subject: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
question: Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0 by factorising.
response_text:
We need two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to −5: these are −2 and −3.
$$x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0$$
$$\therefore\ x = 2 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -3$$
The parabola therefore crosses the x-axis at two points.

faults.note: stem-sol membership: x = −3 gives (−3)² − 5(−3) + 6 = 30, not 0. From (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 the roots are 2 and 3; the sign of the second was flipped. [computed: p(-3) = 30 -> not a root]

correct_steps: multiply to 6 and add to −5: these are −2 and −3
